body:
N-23b, the part that is NOT built (14 Nov 2026). What part A did: the phone's own library finds an artist/album/song whose name is a letter or two off (LANDMVRKS for "landmarks"; checked on an emulator 14 Nov). What it cannot do: an artist who is NOT in the library and whom the catalogue (Deezer, asked by the server) does not return for the typo; the phone has nothing to compare against, and per ADR-R38 the client must not call outside services itself.
PROPOSAL (belongs with P2-12, "Search and artist pages come from your own server"): the SERVER does the forgiving, once, for every client. (1) A plain measure of "close enough", the same one for songs, albums and artists: names compared after the existing normalisation (lower case, no accents, no punctuation) and a letter-for-letter edit distance of at most 1 for names up to 5 letters, 2 for longer ones, plus a small table of look-alike glyphs that bands use (V for A or U, 0 for O, 1 for I or L, $ for S, @ for A, K for C) so stylised names are found by the plain spelling. (2) Only when the catalogue answers with fewer than a handful of hits for the typed text, the server asks again with the nearest alternative(s) (the typed text with look-alike glyphs swapped, then the library/known-artist names within the distance) and merges, marking which words it assumed ("Showing results for ..."), never silently replacing the person's words. (3) Never more than two extra catalogue requests per search, cached by the server like any other catalogue answer (no bursts at Deezer). (4) Measured, not guessed: N-16's 40 real searches get a section of 15 typos and look-alikes (Landmvrks/landmarks, Hozier, Ke$ha, P!nk, Sigur Ros, etc.) with the expected hit and the rank it must reach.
NOT TO DO: fuzzy matching on the phone against the catalogue (thin-client rule), a per-keystroke search (rate), a spelling-correction library with a big dictionary (names are not words).
